concepts.def: Meeting needs without harming future generations.
The demand humans place on nature.
Designing out waste and reusing materials.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Sustainability — a core area of A-Level Environmental Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Sustainability brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Sustainability.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which cycle has no significant atmospheric phase?
options: Carbon
Nitrogen
Phosphorus
Sulfur

mcqs.q: Average time in a reservoir is called?
options: Flux
Residence time
Lifetime
Half-life

mcqs.q: What does the 'tragedy of the commons' describe?
options: Common land in medieval Britain.
Shared resources tend to be overexploited because individuals benefit personally while sharing costs.
It is a play about poor people.
Decomposition.

mcqs.q: What is the leading driver of global deforestation?
options: Logging for timber and paper.
Decomposition.
Forest fires alone.
Agriculture (especially cattle ranching, soy, palm oil).

mcqs.q: What process moves carbon from the atmosphere into plants?
options: Forest fires alone.
Respiration.
Decomposition.
Photosynthesis.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Anthropogenic perturbation”?
options: Includes volcanic outgassing, biological reduction (DMS) and atmospheric oxidation to sulfate aerosols.
Pathway by which a chemical element moves through biotic and abiotic compartments of Earth.
Average time an element spends in a reservoir = reservoir size / flux.
Human alteration of natural fluxes (e.g., Haber process doubled global reactive N input).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Phosphorus cycle”?
options: Includes volcanic outgassing, biological reduction (DMS) and atmospheric oxidation to sulfate aerosols.
Human alteration of natural fluxes (e.g., Haber process doubled global reactive N input).
Slow, sedimentary cycle: weathering of rocks releases phosphate; runs through life and back to ocean sediments.
Compartment storing a quantity of an element, e.g., ocean carbon, soil nitrogen.
